questions.q: Why compare a LoRA at the same seed?
options: A new seed's own change swamps the LoRA's: 0.49 against 0.087 in the lab
questions.answer: A new seed's own change swamps the LoRA's: 0.49 against 0.087 in the lab
questions.why: At a new seed the off-on difference is about the same as the off-off difference at a new seed. The LoRA's part can't be seen.

questions.q: What does a high pixel difference between off and on prove?
options: That the picture moved a lot, and nothing about whether that's what you wanted
questions.answer: That the picture moved a lot, and nothing about whether that's what you wanted
questions.why: Our harbour pair moves about as far as two unrelated pictures. That measures the size of the change, not its value.

questions.q: Strength is doubled. What is certain?
options: The picture changes twice as much
The change to the weights doubles, while the change in the output may not
questions.answer: The change to the weights doubles, while the change in the output may not
questions.why: The weight's change is linear in strength. The network that follows isn't linear, so the output needn't be.

questions.q: 'LoRA on, no trigger' looks the same as 'LoRA on, with trigger'. What does that suggest?
options: The trigger word isn't doing much, and the LoRA acts whenever it's on
questions.answer: The trigger word isn't doing much, and the LoRA acts whenever it's on
questions.why: Four pictures separate the word's effect from the LoRA's.

questions.q: Why use more than one seed for a verdict?
options: The same LoRA's effect varies a lot from seed to seed: nearly 14-fold in the stand-in
It is required by the sampler
questions.answer: The same LoRA's effect varies a lot from seed to seed: nearly 14-fold in the stand-in
questions.why: One seed can flatter or sink a LoRA. Real models will differ by another amount, so test.
